purpose: Force engineering criticism to target assumptions, evidence, and measurements rather than presentation style.

questions.question: Show the torque calculation.
questions.answer: At 30 kg on a 45 degree slope, F_parallel = m*g*sin(theta) = about 208.1 N. With 0.125 m wheel radius, the ideal total wheel torque to balance gravity is about 26.0 N.m before rolling resistance, skid-steer scrub, drivetrain losses, acceleration, obstacle impacts, unequal wheel loading, and safety margin.
questions.missing_evidence: Motor rated/stall torque curve, drivetrain efficiency, traction coefficient, wheel-load distribution, and loaded ramp measurement.
questions.next_gate: Close motor torque margin from supplier datasheet, then perform instrumented 45 degree loaded test.

questions.question: Why that motor?
questions.answer: DFR-01 selects six Rhino IG52 24 V / 60 rpm / 100 W gearmotors, but the current source set does not contain enough verified motor-curve data to prove the selection margin against the 45 degree load case.
questions.missing_evidence: Authoritative datasheet for rated torque, stall torque/current, gearbox efficiency, thermal limits, shaft loading, and duty cycle.
questions.next_gate: Bind the exact supplier/manufacturer datasheet to the BOM and calculate torque/current/thermal margins before purchase release.

questions.question: Why six wheels?
questions.answer: The selected architecture distributes driven contact across six wheels and uses passive rocker-bogie articulation for uneven terrain while retaining compact skid-steer instead of a separate steering linkage. The competition terrain includes uneven surfaces, bumps up to 30 cm, and a ramp up to 45 degrees.
questions.missing_evidence: Measured wheel-load distribution, obstacle traversal, turning scrub current, and comparison against a simpler four-wheel architecture.
questions.next_gate: CAD/load analysis followed by loaded forward/reverse, turning, obstacle, and ramp tests.

questions.question: What happens on heartbeat loss?
questions.answer: The DFR-01 safety model removes non-zero motion when the command lease expires and removes motor enable when liveness expires. The current software boundary uses 500 ms timeouts. E-stop remains dominant and latched.
questions.missing_evidence: Measured Teensy-to-contactor and wheel stop response on the assembled power stage.
questions.next_gate: Bench-test link loss while logging command age, motor-enable state, contactor state, wheel velocity, and stop time.

questions.question: Where is the centre of mass?
questions.answer: No authoritative centre-of-mass coordinate exists yet. DFR-01 places the payload low and central as a design intent, but without frozen component masses/positions or CAD mass properties, a numerical centre-of-mass claim would be fabricated.
questions.missing_evidence: Frozen CAD mass properties or measured component masses and coordinates, including battery, motors, compute, structure, payload tray, and 1 kg mission object case.
questions.next_gate: Generate CAD mass properties, then confirm as-built balance/scale measurements.

questions.question: How is the payload retained?
questions.answer: DFR-01 specifies a low central 350 x 300 x 180 mm tray with raised sides and tie-down points for the judge-supplied object up to 1 kg.
questions.missing_evidence: Final retention geometry, fastener/tie-down specification, payload-shift limit, and physical loaded traversal evidence.
questions.next_gate: Freeze tray CAD and retain 1 kg through turns, bumps, ramp traversal, and emergency stop.

questions.question: What's your current draw?
questions.answer: The design specifies a 24 V 20 Ah battery, 480 Wh nominal energy, and a 60 A master fuse. Actual rover current draw is not measured. The arithmetic 100 W / 24 V = 4.17 A per motor is valid only if the quoted 100 W is electrical input power; that assumption is not yet verified and must not be presented as expected or stall current.
questions.missing_evidence: Motor datasheet current curve; compute/sensor rail budgets; DC/DC efficiency; idle, cruise, skid-turn, ramp, and stall-adjacent current measurements.
questions.next_gate: Build a source-backed power budget, then log battery and branch currents under defined bench/load conditions.

questions.question: What fails first?
questions.answer: There is no defensible single first-failure claim before hardware tests. Current high-risk hypotheses are traction/slip on severe grade, motor/controller thermal or over-current stress during skid-turn/climb, power protection trip or voltage sag, communications loss, and payload shift. Communications loss is intentionally converted into a safe-stop behavior rather than continued motion.
questions.missing_evidence: Component limits, FMEA ranking, thermal/current telemetry, traction measurements, communication range data, and payload dynamic tests.
questions.next_gate: Create FMEA, rank by severity/occurrence/detectability, then attack highest-risk failure modes first.
